rows.jp: 「おい、反転属性つき勝ち気娘」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hey, unyielding girl with the Reversible Character Attribute!"

rows.jp: 朝のサンドイッチを差し出す。
rows.en: I held out the sandwich from breakfast.

ghs.en: I present her with the sandwich from this morning.

rows.jp: ぽかんと、見つめる冬子。
「んなわけないでしょ！！　サンドイッチでしょ！」
rows.en: “Like hell it is! That’s a sandwich!”

ghs.en: Touko: "'s not that at all you know!!! It's a sandwich you know!"
ghs.assessment: Both source clauses end in でしょ, so repeated you know is motivated. The defects are punctuation and awkward clipping.
ghs.remedy: Keep the repeated tag in clean colloquial English.

highlights.text: Touko: "'s not that at all you know!!! It's a sandwich you know!"

ghs.en: Taichi: "So you do know don't you."

ghs.assessment: 手を払われる says that the narrator's hand is slapped aside. 'A swat of her hands' changes whose body is struck, pluralizes the hand, and leaves a fragment.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She slaps my hand away.'

highlights.text: a swat of her hands,

rows.jp: サンドイッチが落ちた。

ghs.assessment: In clipped narration recovered can mean retrieved or picked up. It is underspecified and objectless, but does not necessarily describe recuperation.
ghs.remedy: Use I picked it up.

highlights.text: recovered.

ghs.assessment: そっぽを向く describes her physically turning her face away. 'Uncooperative' replaces the visible action with a generalized judgment.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She turns away.'

highlights.text: Uncooperative.

rows.jp: 「自分しか、自分の心配をしてくれる人間がいないのは、つらいだろ？」
rows.en: “It’s rough when the only person looking out for you is yourself, isn’t it?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Having no human alive, none outside of you, that worry about you... it's painful, right?"
ghs.assessment: The English's nested negatives and plural agreement do not form a grammatical statement of the source's point: it is painful when the only person looking after you is yourself.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It's hard when the only person who will worry about you is you, isn't it?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Having no human alive, none outside of you, that worry about you... it's painful, right?"

rows.jp: 「何言ってるのかわからない」
rows.en: “I have no idea what you’re talking about.”

ghs.en: Touko: "What's that even mean I don't know."
ghs.assessment: The English splices a question and 'I don't know' without a conjunction or punctuation. The source simply says she does not understand what he is talking about.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I don't know what you're talking about.'

highlights.text: Touko: "What's that even mean I don't know."

rows.en: “You want someone to worry about you.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You want people to worry about you."

rows.jp: 「俺、ちょっとは心配なんだけどな」
rows.en: “I do worry about you a little, you know.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And me, I'm getting somewhat worried here."

rows.en: She fixed me with a glare.

rows.jp: 「心配してるなら、どうして、どうしてっ！」
rows.en: “If you’re so worried, then why? Why?!”

ghs.en: Touko: "If you're worried, then why, why!"

rows.jp: 「あ、今は別に怒らせようとか思ってないんだけど」
rows.en: “I mean, I’m not actually trying to make you angry right now.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah, but I'm not really thinking of trying to anger you or anything right now."

ghs.assessment: よろめく is a complete clipped action, 'I stagger.' 'Staggering' is an unattached participle.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I stagger.'

highlights.text: Staggering.

rows.en: It didn’t hurt in the least.

ghs.en: That did not hurt in the slightest.

rows.jp: 冬子は攻撃したあと、へたりこんでいた。
rows.en: Touko crumpled to the floor after striking me.

ghs.en: Right after this strike, Touko collapses sitting on to the floor.

rows.jp: 目頭を押さえて、青い顔をしている。
rows.en: She was pale, pressing one hand to the inner corner of her eye.

ghs.en: Holding her eyes shut, her face almost colorless.
ghs.assessment: 目頭 is the inner corner of the eye. The source says she presses there; it does not say that she holds both eyes shut.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She presses the inner corner of her eye, her face pale.'

highlights.text: Holding her eyes shut, her face almost colorless.

ghs.en: Touko: "Don't address me without honorifics, you..."
So she says as if squeezing it out.

rows.jp: 一瞬で、額に汗が浮いていた。
rows.en: Sweat beaded across her forehead in an instant.

ghs.en: In that moment, sweat surfaces on her forehead.

rows.jp: 「こんな状況なんだぞ。休戦だ」
rows.en: “Look at the situation we’re in. Truce.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Things are like this, OK? Truce."

rows.jp: もう医者はいないのだから。

ghs.en: Because there are no doctors anymore, now.

ghs.assessment: ぞっとする is the narrator's reaction of feeling a chill or horror. 'She's shivering' assigns a visible physical action to Tōko instead.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A chill runs through me.'

highlights.text: She's shivering.

rows.jp: 「気持ち悪い。ふらふらする……吐きそう」
rows.en: “I feel sick. Dizzy... like I’m going to throw up.”

ghs.en: Touko: "I feel nauseous. I feel dizzy... like to throw up."
ghs.assessment: 'Like to throw up' is not grammatical after 'I feel.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'I feel nauseated and dizzy... I think I'm going to throw up.'

highlights.text: Touko: "I feel nauseous. I feel dizzy... like to throw up."

rows.en: I motioned for her to lie down.

ghs.assessment: 促す is the narrator's action of urging her. 'Urgently' is an adverb fragment and changes the action into a manner.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I urge her to.'

highlights.text: Urgently.

rows.jp: 冬子は抵抗しなかった。

ghs.assessment: 冬子は抵抗しなかった means that Tōko did not resist. 'Had no resistance' is an unnatural nominal recasting.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Tōko did not resist.'

highlights.text: Touko had no resistance.

ghs.en: Is this just loss of eyesight?
ghs.assessment: The following source line explicitly treats blindness as the better outcome, so just anticipates a minimization present in context. The defect is awkward grammar.
ghs.remedy: Express the same bleak minimization naturally.

highlights.text: Is this just loss of eyesight?

rows.en: If that was all, it was still the better outcome.

rows.jp: 重篤な疾患や、臓器におよぶ大怪我よりはマシだ。
rows.en: Better than a grave illness or an injury to her internal organs.

ghs.en: Anything is preferable to serious illnesses, or external damage that reaches internal organs.
ghs.assessment: 大怪我 is a major injury, not 'external damage.' The source compares blindness with grave disease or injury extending to the organs.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It would be better than a grave illness or a major injury involving her organs.'

highlights.text: Anything is preferable to serious illnesses, or external damage that reaches internal organs.

rows.jp: 「冷静にね。パニックにならないで」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Stay composed, OK? Don't you dare panic."
ghs.assessment: The source calmly tells her not to panic. 'Don't you dare' adds a threatening or scolding force inconsistent with that instruction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Stay calm. Don't panic.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Stay composed, OK? Don't you dare panic."

rows.jp: 「ここ数日、体に異常はあった？」
rows.en: “Have you noticed anything wrong with your body these past few days?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Was there anything out of the ordinary physically in the last few days?"

rows.en: “Did you get some dangerous chemical in your eyes?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Did you get some powerful medicine or something poisonous on the eyes?"

rows.en: Had it really come out of nowhere?

ghs.en: Really all of a sudden then.

rows.jp: 「ちょっと見えるようになってきた」

ghs.en: Touko: "I think I'm starting to see something now."

ghs.assessment: The source tentatively concludes 'Then it's anemia.' 'Just' adds minimization not present in the diagnosis.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Then it's anemia.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Then this was just anemia."

rows.jp: 「そういう症状が出ることがあるんだ。気持ち悪いのもそのせいだな」
rows.en: “It can cause symptoms like that. It would explain the nausea too.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The symptoms seem to be all there. It should also cause your feeling of nausea."
ghs.assessment: The source says anemia can produce symptoms like these and that it also explains the nausea. 'The symptoms seem to be all there' instead claims a complete diagnostic checklist is present.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Anemia can cause symptoms like that. It would explain the nausea too.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "The symptoms seem to be all there. It should also cause your feeling of nausea."

rows.jp: 無言は非肯定を意味していた。
冬子はゆっくりと上体を起こす。

rows.en: “...I never have an appetite in summer.”

ghs.assessment: The omitted topic is appetite: she says she never has one in summer. 'Never in Summer' is an incomplete fragment that does not state what is absent.
ghs.remedy: Use '...I never have an appetite in summer.'

highlights.text: Touko: "...never in Summer."

rows.jp: 「でも貧血が起きるのはまずいよ、先生」
rows.en: “But passing out from anemia is no good, Professor Kirihara.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But an attack of anemia is bad, Sensei!"
ghs.assessment: If 先生 is retained rather than functionally translated, standard Hepburn is sensei in lowercase, not the capitalized unglossed 'Sensei.'
ghs.remedy: Use a functional joking address such as 'doctor' or consistent standard Hepburn.

highlights.text: Taichi: "But an attack of anemia is bad, Sensei!"

rows.jp: 「神話の中で、砂と魔女を挟んで食べたのが由来なんだ」
rows.en: “The name comes from an old myth: people ate witches sandwiched between layers of sand.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "According to the legends, it was eaten sandwiched between sand and a witch, and that is the origin of its name."

rows.jp: 由来＆語源主義的な浅薄スノッブ連中がだまされそうなナイスガセである。
rows.en: A first-rate fake etymology—just plausible enough to fool shallow snobs obsessed with origins and word roots.

ghs.en: A most nice bit of nonsense to deceive the shallow etymologies & legends snobs.
ghs.assessment: 由来＆語源主義的 describes shallow snobs obsessed with origins and etymologies. 'Etymologies & legends snobs' is ungrammatical and changes the first category to legends.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A fine piece of nonsense for fooling shallow origin-and-etymology snobs.'

highlights.text: A most nice bit of nonsense to deceive the shallow etymologies & legends snobs.

rows.jp: 冬子は目頭をこすった。
rows.en: Touko rubbed the corner of her eye.

ghs.en: Touko rubs around her eye sockets.

ghs.assessment: The singular possessive subject calls for 'your eyes,' not 'the eyes' with singular agreement.
ghs.remedy: Use 'How are your eyes?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "How's the eyes?"

rows.jp: 冬子の手が、じりじりと水位があがるように、それをつかんだ。
rows.en: Touko’s hand crept upward like a rising tide and closed around it.

ghs.en: Touko's hand went up, slow and steady like the rising of the waterline, and seized it.

rows.jp: ツッコミにも力がない。
rows.en: Even her retort had no strength behind it.

ghs.en: Even her straight-man has no strength.
ghs.assessment: ツッコミ is her retort or straight-man response. 'Her straight-man' incorrectly labels the person and omits the response itself.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Even her retort is feeble.'

highlights.text: Even her straight-man has no strength.

ghs.en: Taichi: "This is hand-made, I'll have you know."

rows.jp: わさわさとラップをむいて、小さく齧(かじ)りついた。
rows.en: She rustled open the plastic wrap and took a small bite.

ghs.en: Fidgeting she removed the wrap, then took a little nibble.

ghs.assessment: The singular sandwich was made that morning. 'They're this morning's' changes the number and leaves the intended explanation unnatural.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I made it this morning.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "They're this morning's."

ghs.en: Touko: "It's too big and hard to eat."
Taichi: "I really like 'em harsh and spicy."

rows.en: Apparently it killed her to admit it.
She clapped a hand over her mouth.

ghs.assessment: 口元を押さえる means to cover or press a hand to one's mouth. 'Clamps down her mouth' describes forcibly closing the mouth itself.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She covers her mouth.'

highlights.text: She clamps down her mouth.

ghs.assessment: 首を振る is a complete action by Tōko. 'Shake of the head' is an unattached noun fragment.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She shakes her head.'

highlights.text: Shake of the head.

rows.jp: 無理して、嚥下(えんげ)した。

ghs.en: Taichi: "An essential in a fallen world."

rows.en: she put her lips directly to the rim

ghs.en: she puts it to the mouth,
then raises the canteen's butt to the sky.

rows.jp: 喉が隆起して、水分を摂取する。旺盛に。
rows.en: Her throat bobbed as she drank. With gusto.

ghs.en: Her throat giving protuberance as water passes through. Vigorously.
ghs.assessment: The source describes her throat bobbing as she drinks vigorously. 'Giving protuberance as water passes through' is ungrammatical and substitutes an anatomical abstraction for the visible action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Her throat bobs as she drinks, voraciously.'

highlights.text: Her throat giving protuberance as water passes through. Vigorously.

rows.jp: 「……水分くらい補給してるわけ？」
rows.en: “...Have you at least been drinking enough?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...you're not replenishing your fluids regularly?"

rows.jp: 「帰る途中で転んで、坂の下に全部落ちた」
rows.en: “I fell on the way home and dropped everything down the hill.”

ghs.en: Touko: "They fell on the way home, and rolled all the way to the bottom of a hill."
ghs.assessment: Tōko says that she fell on the way home and dropped everything down the hill. 'They fell' omits her fall and assigns the entire event to the supplies.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I fell on the way home and dropped everything down the hill.'

highlights.text: Touko: "They fell on the way home, and rolled all the way to the bottom of a hill."

ghs.assessment: The Japanese speaker metadata identifies Taichi as the speaker. The English labels the teasing line as Tōko.
ghs.remedy: Attribute the line to Taichi.

highlights.text: Touko: "Clumsy-chan I'm gonna call ya."

rows.jp: 「店に取りに戻ればいいだろうが」

ghs.en: Taichi: "You could've just returned to the store and taken more."

rows.jp: 「……そしたらまたあのメモ書かないといけなくなるから」
rows.en: “...Then I’d have to leave another note.”

ghs.en: Touko: "...but then I would just have to write another memo and then,"
Touko: "if people were to see it..."

rows.en: All this just to save face?

ghs.en: It's only a question of honor?

rows.en: She was on the verge of tears.

ghs.en: She became as if to cry.
ghs.assessment: 泣きそうになる means that she looks or begins to feel as though she may cry. 'Became as if to cry' is not idiomatic English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She looks ready to cry.'

highlights.text: She became as if to cry.

rows.jp: 「はー、桐原先生、そりゃ呆けすぎですぜ」
rows.en: “Honestly, Professor Kirihara. You’re taking clueless to a whole new level.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ohhh, Kirihara-sensei, you are acting too much like the funny man in a comedy duo you are!"
ghs.assessment: 呆けすぎ criticizes her as far too absent-minded or foolish. The English forces a comedy-duo 'funny man' explanation into the line and then repeats 'you are.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'Kirihara-sensei, that was far too absent-minded.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ohhh, Kirihara-sensei, you are acting too much like the funny man in a comedy duo you are!"

rows.jp: 「人がいなくなったら、そんな価値観は消える」
rows.en: “Once everyone else is gone, those values go with them.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If there's no people anymore, then the recognition of values like that disappears."
ghs.assessment: 価値観 means the values themselves. 'The recognition of values' adds a perceiving act and changes what disappears.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Once people are gone, values like that disappear.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "If there's no people anymore, then the recognition of values like that disappears."

rows.jp: 何も許容されなくなる。
それは純粋な個としての人。
rows.en: The human being, stripped down to the pure individual.

ghs.en: That is a person existing in pure Individuality.

rows.jp: あらゆる欲望が、蔑まれさえしていた欲求に簒奪(さんだつ)される。
rows.en: Every desire is usurped by needs once held in contempt.

ghs.en: All desires are being usurped by the previously scorned wants.

rows.jp: 冬子にそれがあるとは思えない。
rows.en: I couldn’t imagine Touko having that kind of strength.

ghs.en: I didn't think those wants were in Touko.
ghs.assessment: それ refers to the strength to live named immediately before, not to the earlier desires. 'Those wants were in Tōko' binds the pronoun to the wrong concept.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I can't imagine Tōko possesses that strength.'

highlights.text: I didn't think those wants were in Touko.

rows.jp: とうに、わかっていたことだ。
rows.en: I had known it all along.

ghs.en: They are something that I discovered, long ago.
ghs.assessment: The source says 'I had known it for a long time.' 'They are something that I discovered' invents a plural subject and changes settled knowledge into discovery.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I had known it for a long time.'

highlights.text: They are something that I discovered, long ago.

rows.jp: こいつはもう限界なんだって。
rows.en: She had already reached her limit.

ghs.en: This gal's already at the limit.

rows.jp: 人類が滅亡して、家族もいなくなって、あの広い屋敷みたいな家で。
rows.en: With humanity gone, her family gone, alone in that sprawling mansion of a house—

ghs.en: Mankind fallen, her family also gone, and in that enormous castle-like mansion...

rows.jp: 「……これから、八人だけで生きていかないといけないんだぞ」
rows.en: “From now on, the eight of us have to find a way to survive.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...from now on, we're going to have to make do and live with only eight of us."

rows.jp: 誰にだって、逃れられない死が待ってる。
rows.en: Death awaits everyone. No one escapes it.

ghs.en: Death is an inescapable eventuality for everyone.

rows.jp: 「問題はいつ、どう死ぬかだろ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "The problem is when one dies, and how."

rows.jp: 「こんな……ありえないじゃない……人が……いなくなるなんて」
rows.en: “This can’t... This can’t be real... People can’t just... disappear.”

ghs.en: Touko: "This... can't be can it... people are just... not there anymore."

rows.en: I forced her to face it.

rows.jp: 「世界は人を塗りつぶした。俺たちだけが、『互い』だ」
rows.en: “The world has painted everyone else out. Now we’re all each other has.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "This world has painted out all people. We alone are... reciprocal."
ghs.assessment: 俺たちだけが『互い』だ says that the survivors are now one another's only others or counterparts. 'We alone are reciprocal' is not idiomatic and fails to communicate that human relation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'We are all each other has.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "This world has painted out all people. We alone are... reciprocal."

rows.jp: 仕方、ないのかもしれない。
rows.en: Maybe there was no avoiding it.
I had chosen to get involved.

ghs.en: There was involvement. A wish for it.
ghs.assessment: 関わったのだ。望んで states that the narrator chose to become involved. 'There was involvement. A wish for it' removes the acting and choosing subject.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I got involved because I wanted to.'

highlights.text: There was involvement. A wish for it.

rows.jp: 俺が冬子と築きたかった関係は、決して蜂蜜のようなそれではなかったけれど。
rows.en: The relationship I had wanted with Touko was never meant to be anything honey-sweet.

ghs.en: The relationship I wanted to build with Touko was never to be in any way similar to honey, but...

rows.jp: この壊れかけの少女を、放置するという選択はない。
rows.en: But abandoning a girl already coming apart was not an option.

ghs.en: ...the choice to abandon this broken girl to herself will never appear.
ghs.assessment: The source says leaving this damaged girl alone is not an option. 'The choice ... will never appear' turns the narrator's decision into an event that may or may not materialize.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Leaving this damaged girl alone is not an option.'

highlights.text: ...the choice to abandon this broken girl to herself will never appear.

rows.en: Up to a point, that was fine.

ghs.en: Up to partway through it's fine.
But... what about the very final part?

rows.jp: もう逃げ場はないに違いない。
rows.en: There would be nowhere left to run.

ghs.en: There are no more places to escape to, no mistake.

rows.jp: 冬子ルートとも言うべき流れに乗って、際まで行って、そこで全てが崩壊したとしても。
rows.en: Even if I followed what might as well be called the Touko route all the way to the brink, only for everything to collapse there—

ghs.en: Even if I ride this flow that ought be called the Touko Route, even if I go all the way to the edge, even if nothing is there but Downfall...
ghs.assessment: 全てが崩壊した says that everything may collapse at the end. 'Nothing is there but Downfall' changes the event into an abstract destination and adds capitalization.
ghs.remedy: Use '...even if everything collapses when I reach the end.'

highlights.text: Even if I ride this flow that ought be called the Touko Route, even if I go all the way to the edge, even if nothing is there but Downfall...

rows.jp: 今度はその終焉までつきあわないといけない。
rows.en: this time, I would have to stay with it to the very end.

ghs.en: This time, not going together to that demise will be impossible.
ghs.assessment: The narrator says he must see it through with her to its end. The English's double negative makes that commitment opaque.
ghs.remedy: Use 'This time, I have to stay with her until the very end.'

highlights.text: This time, not going together to that demise will be impossible.

rows.jp: 爛熟という苦痛に苛まれながら。
rows.en: Tormented by the agony of overripeness.

ghs.en: While being hailed torment by the agony that is this over-ripeness.
ghs.assessment: 苛まれながら means while being tormented by the pain called over-ripeness. 'Being hailed torment' has no grammatical or semantic relation to that construction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Tormented all the while by the pain of overripeness.'

highlights.text: While being hailed torment by the agony that is this over-ripeness.

rows.jp: 「どうしても耐えられないなら」

ghs.en: Taichi: "If whatever you do it remains unbearable..."

rows.jp: 敏感に冬子が反応した。
rows.en: Touko seized on the words at once.

ghs.assessment: The lexical and adverbial relation is blurred, but the underlying event remains identifiable.
ghs.remedy: Restore the precise relation in natural English.

highlights.text: Touko's response is sensible.

rows.en: “...If I can’t bear it, then what?”

ghs.assessment: The Japanese speaker metadata identifies Tōko as the speaker asking him to finish the conditional. The English assigns the line to Taichi.
ghs.remedy: Attribute the line to Tōko.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...whatever I do, what?"

rows.jp: 「いや、それ、全部食べていいから」
rows.en: “No. I mean, you can finish the whole thing.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "No, well, it's fine if you eat it all."

rows.jp: サンドイッチを囓りながら冬子。

ghs.en: Touko was still nibbling on her sandwich.

rows.jp: 「どうして、人は滅びたんだと思う？」
rows.en: “Why do you think humanity died out?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "What do you think annihilated humanity?"
ghs.assessment: The proposition survives; the defect is a small shift in what the question places in focus.
ghs.remedy: Keep the source question focus.

highlights.text: Taichi: "What do you think annihilated humanity?"

rows.jp: 何を期待して問うたわけでもない。
rows.en: I had not expected an answer.

ghs.en: It wasn't a question I expected an answer for.

ghs.assessment: The event survives, but the English destabilizes who frames or experiences it.
ghs.remedy: Restore the source subject framing.

highlights.text: Touko: "This isn't annihilation, no."

rows.jp: とんでもなく哲学的な答えが戻ってきた。
rows.en: The answer that came back was wildly philosophical.

rows.jp: 「……薄くなって消えてしまったのよ」

ghs.en: Touko: "...they've just thinned out until they were gone."
